title: Unacknowledged suggestions influenced AI reasoning through question and filler tokens
summary: Researchers found that activation changes at questions and filler tokens carried part of an unacknowledged suggestion’s influence in two language models. Swapping those native activations partially shifted the models’ next-token predictions toward the predictions made without the suggestion.
organization: University of Wisconsin-Madison; University of Oxford

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 causal analysis §§4.1–4.2, Figures 5–7 and matched token controls

evidence.tested: The two-target patch recovered 16.2% of the counterfactual distribution shift in Gemma and 19.3% in the DeepSeek model, measured by the study’s KL-divergence recovery metric. Equal-size random token controls recovered less.
evidence.unknown: The experiment concerns held-fixed responses under the tested suggestions. It establishes partial mediation at the selected locations, with effects that differ by model.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted residual stream editor identified candidate locations where hidden representations preserve a suggestion’s influence, which researchers tested with independent native activation patching.
